slides.1.title: Key Information on the Label
slides.1.html:
📋 Mandatory Information

  • Wine category: Vinho Tinto (red) / Vinho Branco (white) / Vinho Rosado (rosé)
  • Alcohol content: shown as % vol.
  • Volume: usually 750ml
  • Origin: Produto de Portugal (product of Portugal)
  • Producer: the name of the estate or merchant

📋 Common Terms

  • Denominação de Origem Controlada: the DOC legally defined appellation
  • Quinta (estate) / Herdade (estate): a single-estate wine
  • Colheita (vintage): the harvest year
  • Reserva: a select grade (defined differently by each DOC, usually requiring longer ageing)
  • Grande Reserva: the highest select grade
  • LBV (Late Bottled Vintage): a special Port term
slides.2.question: What does "Vinho Tinto" on a Portuguese label mean?
slides.2.explanation: In Portuguese: Tinto = red (red wine), Branco = white (white wine), Rosado = rosé (rosé wine), Espumante = sparkling (sparkling wine).
slides.3.message: Congratulations on completing Lesson 6! You have mastered the basics of reading a Portuguese wine label.
slides.3.keyPoints.0: Vinho Tinto = red, Branco = white, Rosado = rosé
slides.3.keyPoints.1: Quinta / Herdade = estate, indicating a single origin
slides.3.keyPoints.2: Reserva / Grande Reserva = select grades of higher quality
slides.3.keyPoints.3: The DOC name is the most important quality indicator
